title: Oncall context strip and visual anchors - notes for dashboard handoff
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This note captures a lightweight pattern we want to trial for making dashboards and alerts immediately actionable for first responders. Two primitives: 1) a compact "context strip" that sits at the top of each major dashboard and in alert messages; 2) a set of "visual anchors" (small, consistent widget affordances and badges) that let an operator jump from symptom -> provenance -> reproduction steps in under a minute.

Why this helps (problem statement):
- Operators spend too long collecting the basic facts for every incident: what changed, which tenants affected, which model variant was used, whether cache warmed, and if fallbacks fired.
- Traces and metrics exist, but their entry points are inconsistent across dashboards.
- We want fast triage with minimal cognitive load so runbooks are followed and noisy paging is reduced.

Design: Context strip (top-of-dashboard header) - fields and semantics:
- one-line incident summary (derived from alert) -> "ALERT: high token tail latency / spike in TTF token for hosted-api"
- severity (S0..S3) mapped to sampling policy and escalation path
- span/trace id anchor: single clickable id that opens trace replay view
- affected cohort: human readable ("10 tenants, top: acme-inc, beta-corp")
- key hypothesis tags: comma-separated tags such as model_variant=redwood-2-8b, kv_warmth=20%, fallback=enabled
- quick next-step (1 sentence) -> "Check model fallback count & last successful KV prime"
- owner/rotation contact quick link (pager or Slack channel)

Visual anchors (widget conventions):
- Anchor badge: small colored badge in widget title showing provenance tag (e.g., PURPLE=tracing-anchored, ORANGE=derived metric, GREY=synthetic probe)
- Trace jump: every latency/response-time panel must show the top 1 trace ids for that slice in a short list (top 3) with direct links
- Cohort toggles: tenant/route toggle in the same horizontal area as the widget so the operator can switch context without hunting
- Warmth strip: a micro-gauge shown beside KV cache rate panels showing percent warm for the last 5m and 1h

Span / trace tag mapping for UI anchors (recommended canonical tag set):
- tenant_id -> used for cohort filtering and owner lookup
- route_id -> maps to API route + product feature (shows route config link)
- model_variant -> used to show model-level fallback/quantization profile
- kv_warmth_pct -> shown in the warmth strip and used for cold-start hypothesis
- batch_size_hint -> helps correlate throughput/latency changes
- fallback_reason -> maps to fallback badge and to the fallback metrics panel
- sampling_label -> indicates why trace was captured (synthetic, severity-sampled, cohort-sampled)

Sampling and retention guidance (practical):
- Severity-based adaptive sampling: S0/S1 -> 100% capture for 10m window then 20% for next hour. S2 -> 5% sample by default but escalate on rate increase. S3 -> only errors and synthetic probes by default.
- Cohort-triggered amplification: if a tenant's error rate doubles in 3m, switch that tenant to 50% trace capture for 30m.
- Redaction rules: PII fields removed at ingestion; tenant_id replaced with hashed alias in public dashboards.

First-responder mini-runbook (0-6 min reproducibility path):
1) Read context strip header: severity, hypothesis, owner link. If severity S0/S1, page immediately.
2) Click top trace id shown in the latency panel (opens trace viewer with annotated spans). Note model_variant and batch hints.
3) Check "Warmth strip" and KV prefetch rate: if kv_warmth_pct < 40% -> mark cold-start hypothesis.
4) Look at fallback badge and fallback count time series; if fallback spikes, follow fallback_reason tag to model variant mismatch or OOM.
5) If cohort shows small number of tenants, use tenant toggle to isolate and run stored prompt replay for that tenant (link in context strip).
6) If reproduction is successful, annotate trace with reproduction label and link to Jira/CON page; escalate if S0/S1.

Metrics validation checklist (quick):
- Is the metric using canonical labels (tenant_id, route_id, model_variant)?
- Is the aggregation consistent with SLO (percentile vs mean)?
- Are derived metrics computed server-side or in dashboards (note in header)?
- Does the widget include trace jump list (yes/no)?

Ownership and operational rules:
- Dashboard context strip content authored by owning service team (serving-runtime or hosted-api), validated by obs team before rollout.
- Sampling policy rules live in obs-config repo (CON-1428); dashboard teams must not override without change request.
- When creating a new metric, include a one-line "consumer intent" annotation in the metric description (who uses it and for which SLO).

Micro-UX examples and placement notes:
- Keep context strip height minimal: two lines max. Top line is alert summary + severity; second line is quick actions and links.
- Use compact icons to indicate clickable elements (trace, ticket, slack). Avoid long URLs in header.
- Widgets should reserve a right-column area for micro-actions: "open top trace" / "open tenant replay" / "open config".

Open questions / TODOs (experiments to run):
- How noisy will trace-links be on high-traffic dashboards? (experiment: enable trace lists only when alert triggers)
- Best representation for tenant anonymity on public dashboards while preserving actionable owner info inside private dashboards
- UX test: can a new responder follow runbook in under 3 minutes? Run a tabletop with 4 engineers.

Quick references and links:
- CON-1428: sampling policy and adaptive-sampling RFC
- JIRA-OPS-388: dashboard handoff pilot
- PR: obs-dashboards#224 - initial context strip implementation (WIP)

Notes to self / informal brain-dump:
- Try to keep tags minimal. The UI should present 3–5 salient tags in context strip, with a secondary expand for full metadata.
- Consider a small "repro button" that triggers a sandboxed prompt replay using stored inputs for the selected tenant (requires permissions gating).
- If fallback_reason is present, auto-expand fallback panel on open so operator doesn't miss it.

End of draft.

Feedback requested from: serving-runtime, hosted-api product owners, ops oncall rota leads.
